boring_rival_explanations: Subjects with high HRV have longer stable calibration segments, leading to more accurate quantile estimates and thus higher coverage.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Higher baseline HRV leads to higher empirical coverage (positive direction) or no change.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After matching subjects on fitness level and stress reactivity, the association between baseline HRV and coverage disappears.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Need to measure fitness via VO2max test and baseline stress reactivity via task-evoked HRV change.

boring_rival_explanations: Motion artifact periods are automatically excluded from analysis, leaving only clean data that yields nominal coverage.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Increased motion artifact leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because the nonconformity score captures increased error, widening intervals.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: When artifact-contaminated segments are retained and analyzed, coverage rises with artifact level; after removing them, coverage returns to baseline.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Attachment quality can be assessed via impedance; BMI from metadata; activity type from accelerometer magnitude.

boring_rival_explanations: Later segments have more data for quantile estimation, reducing sampling error and increasing coverage.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Later recording time leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) due to improved quantile estimation or reduced physiological variance from habituation.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: If calibration is performed with a sliding window matched to test time, coverage does not decline with time; if using fixed early calibration, coverage declines only when confounding fatigue is present.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Fatigue can be measured via psychomotor vigilance task; time of day from timestamps.

boring_rival_explanations: Timestamp offsets correlate with poor signal quality, leading to automatic exclusion of those segments and biasing the sample toward higher coverage.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Larger timestamp offset leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because misalignment adds noise that inflates residuals, widening intervals.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After applying a data-driven time-warping alignment, coverage remains unchanged across offset levels; if offsets are merely a proxy for low SQI, controlling for SQI removes the effect.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Latency jitter can be assessed by comparing simultaneous trigger signals; SQI from peak detection success rates.

boring_rival_explanations: Noisy labels arise primarily during low-signal-quality intervals, which are filtered out, leaving a cleaner subset with nominal coverage.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Higher label noise entropy leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because the model receives more uncertain targets, increasing conformity scores and widening intervals.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: When using a loss function robust to label noise (e.g., label smoothing), coverage does not deteriorate with increasing label entropy; if the effect is due to exclusion of low-quality segments, controlling for signal quality removes the association.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Expertise can be scored via years of experience; stimulus clarity from protocol notes.

possible_confounders: number of stress episodes per subject
boring_rival_explanations: Low-baseline subjects tend to have fewer stress episodes, resulting in smaller calibration sets that actually drive undercoverage; the apparent baseline effect is confounded by calibration size.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Lower baseline arousal leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because low baseline subjects exhibit less physiological variability, yielding more stable residuals.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After stratifying by calibration set size, the relationship between baseline arousal and coverage vanishes; if baseline truly matters, adjusting for baseline via subject-specific centering equalizes coverage across baseline groups.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Baseline noise estimated from test-retest reliability of pre-stimulus period; episode count from annotation.

boring_rival_explanations: Subjects with few calibration samples also have shorter recordings, which exhibit less temporal drift, thus showing nominal or higher coverage despite small sample size.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Smaller calibration set size leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) due to the conservative bias of the standard split conformal quantile for small n.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: When using an unbiased quantile estimator (e.g., smoothed or exact binomial), coverage does not increase with decreasing calibration size; if the effect is due to shorter recordings, controlling for total duration removes the association.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Recording length from timestamps; labeling consistency from inter-annotator agreement.

boring_rival_explanations: Subjects with strong GSR-temperature coupling also exhibit higher motion artifacts, which independently cause undercoverage; the interaction effect is confounded by motion.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Stronger GSR-temperature interaction leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because the linear scoring function already captures sufficient variance, and adding interaction would overfit, widening intervals.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After adding the interaction term to the scoring function, coverage does not improve (or worsens) for high-interaction subjects; if motion is the true driver, controlling for artifact level abolishes the interaction-coverage link.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: GSR amplitude from std of phasic component; temperature range from min-max during stress; artifact level as in H2.

boring_rival_explanations: Substance users are more likely to be younger and have higher baseline HRV, which independently affect coverage; the substance effect is confounded by age and baseline physiology.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Presence of caffeine/medication leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because substances stabilize autonomic responses, reducing variance and improving calibration.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: After adjusting for baseline physiological state (e.g., subtracting substance-induced baseline shift) and age, the association between substance intake and coverage disappears; if substances truly alter error distribution, controlling for baseline will not remove the effect.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Time of day from timestamps; baseline stress from first 5 min; age from metadata.

possible_confounders: feature extraction method (e.g., mean vs percentile)
boring_rival_explanations: Short stress bouts are more often ambiguously labeled, leading to label noise that drives undercoverage; the window edge effect is confounded by label quality.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Shorter bout length relative to window leads to higher empirical coverage (or no change) because windowed features are smoothed, reducing variance and widening intervals.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: When using variable-length windows matched to each bout duration, coverage does not differ across bout lengths; if label ambiguity is the true cause, controlling for label ambiguity removes the bout-length-coverage association.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Label ambiguity from entropy of multiple annotators; bout duration from annotation epochs; feature method from pipeline config.
